blocks.html: Travel is one of the most visual and time-sensitive things a person ever buys — yet most agencies and online travel platforms still confirm trips and chase enquiries with plain text nobody looks forward to opening. Rich messaging changes that: a verified, branded conversation with photos, carousels and tap-to-act buttons that arrives inside the traveler's default messaging app, with no extra download in the way.

This guide walks through how tour operators, online travel platforms and hospitality teams put RCS messaging to work across the whole journey — from the first enquiry to post-trip loyalty — and why travel messaging built on rich cards handles booking confirmations, flight status updates and last-minute changes without a single grainy SMS. Ojiva AI runs it on the same dashboard as WhatsApp and SMS, so book a free demo to see it mapped against your own booking flow.

sections.heading: Why Rich Messaging Fits the Way Travel Brands Sell

blocks.html: Travel decisions are made on feeling — a beach at sunset, a room with a view, a fare that won't last. Plain text can convey none of that, which is why so much travel outreach underperforms the product it is selling. Rich messaging for travel brands closes that gap by putting the trip itself in front of the traveler, not just a description of it.

items.desc: rich cards for travel brands carry destination photos, room galleries and short clips inside the thread itself, instead of a link the traveler has to trust and tap away to see.

items.title: A named sender, not an unknown number:
items.desc: the agency or brand name and logo sit on every message, so an enquiry follow-up reads as the company the traveler actually contacted rather than a suspicious cold text.

items.title: One tap does the work:

sections.heading: Getting Started With RCS for Travel Agencies and Tour Operators in India

blocks.html: The infrastructure is already in place. Jio, Airtel and Vi all support RCS at the network level, and Apple has enabled it on iPhones since iOS 18, so a campaign reaches both Android and iPhone travelers. Where a specific device or network can't render the rich format, the message falls back to standard SMS, so nationwide reach holds.
Setup is a dashboard workflow, not a developer project — and, importantly, it does not use the same registration path as SMS.

items.q: How does RCS messaging work for a travel company?
items.a: It upgrades ordinary text into a branded, app-like conversation inside the traveler's default messaging app — carrying photos, carousels, tappable buttons and a verified sender name. A travel brand connects through a provider like Ojiva AI, gets its sender verified, and can then send booking confirmations, itinerary and check-in reminders and rich offers, all with automatic SMS fallback wherever the rich format isn't supported.

items.q: What's the difference between RCS and SMS for travel booking notifications?
items.a: A standard SMS is plain text with no branding, images or buttons. For travel booking notifications, RCS adds the brand's verified name and logo, shows the fare, room or itinerary as a rich card, and lets the traveler act in one tap. When a device or network can't display the rich version, it simply falls back to SMS, so nothing is lost.

items.q: How is RCS different from WhatsApp for a travel agency?
items.a: Both offer verified, rich, two-way messaging. The practical difference is reach: WhatsApp only lands with travelers who have the app and have opted in, while RCS runs through the phone's native messaging app on supported networks. Many travel agencies use both together and let the system pick whichever will reach a given traveler, rather than choosing one.

items.q: Can travelers book flights and hotels inside a chat message?
items.a: Yes. A rich card can present fare options or room choices with photos and price, and a suggested action opens straight into a secure payment or agent flow — so a traveler goes from browsing to a confirmed booking in one thread. The same mechanism lets a brand recover an abandoned booking by resending the exact option the traveler left behind.

items.q: Do travel businesses need DLT registration to send RCS in India?
items.a: No — DLT registration is a TRAI mechanism specific to SMS. RCS uses a different path: the travel brand is onboarded and verified as a sender through Google's RCS for Business process via the provider, which is what produces the verified badge. Consent and opt-out still matter and should follow DPDP Act principles, but the SMS DLT registration itself does not apply to RCS.

items.q: Which mobile carriers and devices support RCS across India?
items.a: Jio, Airtel and Vi all support RCS at the network level, and Apple has enabled it on iPhones since iOS 18, so campaigns can reach both Android and iPhone travelers. Support depends on the traveler's device and network rather than their city, and any message that can't be delivered as a rich card drops to SMS, so reach stays national.

items.q: How can a travel brand send automated flight delay and check-in updates?
items.a: Connect the messaging channel to the booking or operations system, so a status change — a delay, a gate move, or a check-in window opening — triggers a rich card to the affected travelers automatically. Because it's two-way, a traveler can reply to rebook or reach an agent from the same thread, which cuts the call volume a disruption usually creates.

items.q: How do we get a travel brand verified, and what results can we expect?
items.a: Verification means submitting the business name, logo and category through the provider so the verified sender badge appears from the first message; Ojiva AI manages that review directly. Brands generally see stronger opens and actions than plain SMS because the messages are branded, visual and tappable — which is why rich media campaigns are increasingly used by tour operators, online travel platforms and tourism boards to lift booking conversion.
